text:
SESSION LOCATION RESOLVED. Session does NOT live in the kernel, and k-framecheck's scope shrinks accordingly.

Forced by the dependency graph, not by taste: a checked container useful enough to be worth having must hold recordings AND AOI sets AND grids. aoi dependsOn core, so core cannot see AoiSet; the earliest module that sees all of them is eyes4s-design (dependsOn core, compare -> surface, aoi). Kernel is not even a candidate -- it cannot see Recording.

Split:
  KERNEL (k-framecheck) keeps only the MECHANISM: every operation combining two frame- or clock-carrying values returns Either, using ONE shared identity check rather than a re-inlined comparison per call site. This is already nearly true; what was missing is the sharing -- Interval has a private sameClock while Overlap.selects re-inlines the same comparison, which is eyesim's copy-pasted-predicate seam forming after a single file.

  DESIGN (new bead x-session) gets the CONTAINER: Session validates frame and clock membership on insertion and exposes total accessors, per decision q-scope. It is also the project object APP-13's prerequisite query interrogates from eyes4s-plan.

No conflict with q-scope, which said ergonomics come from a checked container 'at the session layer'. This decision locates that layer.
